title: Intrinsic affine chart completions and generic group stalks of monoschemes
statement: Let $M$ be a fine monoscheme with finite affine cover, and let $C$ be a torsion-free connected component with its canonical generic point $\eta$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Write $S=\mathcal M_\eta$ for its unsharpened monoid stalk and $L=S^{\rm gp}$ for its group completion. Then the canonical map $S\to L$ is a monoid isomorphism. For every nonempty monoid affine open $U$ lying in $C$, the intrinsic section monoid $P_U=\mathcal M(U)$ is fine [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], and there is a group isomorphism $P_U^{\rm gp}\simeq L$ whose value on the canonical image of $p\in P_U$ is the image in $L$ of the germ of $p$ at $\eta$. The assertions quantify over components and hence allow the empty monoscheme; no global torsion-freeness assumption on $M$ is required.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4(i),(iii), 3.1.9 and 3.2.4, printed pp.98--99,103. Intrinsic affine section and generic-stalk part of Step 3 of lem-trf-monoscheme-finite-chart-components.

proof.text: Choose a presentation of U by Spec_mon Q with Q fine. The closed point consists of the nonunits. Its smallest neighbourhood is the whole spectrum: every principal open containing this point is D(a) for a unit a, hence is the whole spectrum. Every covering of this affine open has a member equal to the whole open, so the sheafification unit is bijective on its sections (local surjectivity supplies a representative on that member, and local injectivity gives uniqueness). Constant numerator sections identify these sections with Q, since localization at the unit face changes nothing. Transport along the chart isomorphism to identify the intrinsic section monoid P_U with Q. Finite generation and injectivity into the group completion are invariant under this monoid isomorphism, so P_U is fine.

At the empty prime, apply monoidPrime_minimal_neighborhood to a finite generating tuple of Q. The product a of the generators defines the smallest neighbourhood of the empty prime. Its local-fraction sections are Q localized at a: the inverse of a generator is the product of the other generators divided by a, so this is Q^gp. The smallest-neighbourhood sheafification unit is bijective by the same local representative argument as in Step 1. The empty prime is the generic point in this chart; because the intrinsic component generic point lies in every component chart, T0 uniqueness of the generic point identifies it with eta. Transport the section identification through the chart isomorphism.

A smallest neighbourhood is terminal in the opposite neighbourhood category, so its map to the stalk colimit is an isomorphism (CategoryTheory.Limits.isIso_ι_of_isTerminal). Consequently the stalk S is a group. Its canonical map to S^gp is bijective, with inverse sending a quotient s/t to s times the inverse of t. The germ P_U to S extends uniquely to group completions and is an isomorphism by Step 2. Compose this with S to S^gp. Its value on every numerator p is exactly the defining germ formula for degree. The trivial monoid and the empty generating family give the trivial group; there is no component in the empty case.

lean.statement:
theorem generic_chart_completion (M : Fine.{u})
    (C : ToricComponent M) :
    (∃ e : FineFan.stalk M.space.presheaf C.genericPoint ≃* C.lattice,
      e.toMonoidHom = Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of) ∧
    ∀ U : ComponentAffineOpens C,
      FineFan.IsFine (M.space.presheaf.obj (op U.1.1)) ∧
      ∃ e : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (M.space.presheaf.obj (op U.1.1)) ≃* C.lattice,
        ∀ p, e (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of p) = degree C U p
